# Simple-tile drop-in connector study (generated by study.py)

Tile keeps the rev-A per-tile logic; this study covers the mechanical/contact side only: single PCB, SMD Kailh hot-swap, minimum equilateral lattice (18.36 mm), drop-in chassis, no tile-side MCU/LED/Hall. Acceptance context: 20 MHz shift clock, up to 16 tiles.

## Parameters (inputs; assumptions labelled)

| param | value | note |
|---|---|---|
| key lattice | P = 18.3597 mm, R = 15.900 mm | R = 15.6 body + 0.3 margin; P = R/sin60 (LEDGER 2026-09-27) |
| keys | 12 (3 rows x 4) | row shift P/2 |
| keycap (ASSUMPTION) | custom hexagonal cap, 17.86 mm across flats (lattice Voronoi cell - 0.5 mm) | stock square caps cannot be used at this pitch, see keycap section |
| footprint reach from switch centre | 8.36 mm | parsed from the vendored file |
| edge clearance / outline tol | 0.3 / 0.1 mm | copper-to-edge |
| keep-outs | holes +0.5 mm, pads/courtyard +0.3 mm | revc_edges.py heritage |
| chassis tolerance (ASSUMPTION) | +/-0.35 mm XY | SMT placement + pocket play sum |
| variant A pad (ASSUMPTION) | dia 2.5 mm round | >= spring-tip area + 2*tol; confirm tip dia from DRG-02208 (Harwin drawing) before layout |
| board | 1.6 mm | |

## Tile contact inventory (rev-A interface, not a key matrix)

Derived from docs/architecture/protocol.md (the J101/J102/J103/J104 pin table). All four directions are preserved; B_clk and B_data stay single nets shared by the bottom and right legs, as in rev A:

| direction | pins | nets |
|---|---|---|
| top | 8 | `VCC` (J102.1), `T_clk` (J102.2), `T_data` (J102.3), `T_endcol` (J102.4), `GND` (J102.5), `L_latch` (J102.6), `T_W` (J102.7), `GND` (J102.8) |
| bottom | 8 | `VCC` (J103.1), `B_clk` (J103.2), `B_data` (J103.3), `GND` (J103.4), `B_first` (J103.5), `B_latch` (J103.6), `B_W` (J103.7), `GND` (J103.8) |
| left | 6 | `VCC` (J101.1), `L_clk` (J101.2), `L_data` (J101.3), `L_endrow` (J101.4), `L_latch` (J101.5), `GND` (J101.6) |
| right | 6 | `VCC` (J104.1), `B_clk` (J104.2), `B_data` (J104.3), `GND` (J104.4), `R_latch` (J104.5), `GND` (J104.6) |

**28 tile-side pads, 16 unique nets (14 signals + VCC + GND).** Plus 3 presence straps (6 more pads) below.

## Tile outline (two styles evaluated)

- **stepped**: area 3542.7 mm2, margin 9.18 mm; EdgeTrim pad variant on keys 0,0, 0,1, 0,2
- **rect**: area 4458.1 mm2, margin 8.66 mm; EdgeTrim pad variant on keys 0,2

- Stepped outline: cross-tile key pitch right = 18.360 mm, up = 18.360 mm (target P = 18.360; lattice-continuous = yes). The stepped geometry (G/2 insets on both sides of a 1.0 mm rib gap) follows the rev-C construction in `revc_build.py`; the rev-A/B edge *connector* positions are NOT reused anywhere -- pads sit on interior island lanes. Rect outline trades lattice continuity across the rim for the smallest PCB.

## Keycaps (custom only at this pitch)

- **Hexagonal cap (ASSUMPTION, lattice Voronoi cell - 0.5 mm):** 17.86 mm across flats, area 276.2 mm2; min gap incl. cross-tile neighbours = 0.500 mm. Hex caps are the established answer for isomorphic grids (they tile the triangular lattice exactly).
- Control experiment (review point): a square cap of side P - 0.5 = 17.86 mm OVERLAPS between rows (min gap 0.000 mm): stock square caps are impossible at R = 15.9 mm.
- Largest non-overlapping square cap: 15.40 mm (= R - gap), area 237.2 mm2 - much smaller target than the 17.86-flat hex (276.2 vs 237.2 mm2).

- **stepped**: 28/28 contacts placed in 4 rails (groups: bottom, right, top, left; unresolved: none)
  - rail `bottom` (8 pads) in lane [-26.4, 34.7, 44.6, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 1.45 mm
  - rail `right` (6 pads) in lane [-26.4, 34.7, 44.6, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 1.45 mm
  - rail `top` (8 pads) in lane [-17.1, 19.0, 44.6, 24.5], worst slack after tolerance 1.38 mm
  - rail `left` (6 pads) in lane [-17.1, 19.0, 44.6, 24.5], worst slack after tolerance 1.38 mm
- **rect**: 28/28 contacts placed in 4 rails (groups: bottom, right, top, left; unresolved: none)
  - rail `bottom` (8 pads) in lane [-26.4, 34.7, 63.1, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 1.47 mm
  - rail `right` (6 pads) in lane [-26.4, 34.7, 63.1, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 1.47 mm
  - rail `top` (8 pads) in lane [-26.4, 34.7, 63.1, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 1.47 mm
  - rail `left` (6 pads) in lane [43.6, 28.7, 63.1, 40.0], worst slack after tolerance 0.82 mm

Chassis-side spring body packing (bodies are wider than the pad pitch, so they are staggered into banks; exact all-vs-all body and socket-projection collision checks including the six lattice-neighbour tiles; spring tip anchored on the pad centre - tip offset inside the body is an ASSUMPTION to verify from the part drawing):

- **S1941-42R: NOT PACKABLE** under the study pad plan -> part rejected for this layout; trials: orient 0 banks 4..6, orient 1 banks 2..4.
- **S1971-46R**: packs with 2 bank(s) (along x); 28 contacts placed.

Mating order note: NO first-mate claim is made. With all pad rows coplanar, which contact touches first depends on tilt; guaranteed-first GND would need contact-height staggering (longer GND contacts or stepped pad heights) - recorded as an open mechanical requirement, not solved here.

Vertical budget with Harwin S1941-42R (free 7.3 mm, deflection 0.3-0.8): tile-bottom window [6.5, 7.0] mm above the chassis board; clears the 4.94 mm socket depth BOUND by 1.56 mm. S1971-46R (4.55 mm free) leaves -0.99 mm -> rejected. The socket depth bound is the vendored STEP's raw point extent + 0.5 mm guard with an unverified axis mapping: a worst-case bound, not a nominal clearance; 3D assembly verification is a listed next step.

## Variant B: SMT mezzanine to passive chassis/backplane (scoped)

Contact budget for one connector per tile: 16 unique nets + 6 detection strap endpoints = **22 contacts minimum**. Scope: only the candidates below, all with verified footprints from the installed KiCad 10 library were tested; this says nothing about untested families.

- **df12_pair30** (Hirose_DF12_DF12E3.0-30DP-0.5V_2x15_P0.50mm_Vertical): 30 contacts (need 22); courtyard 10.79 x 6.29 mm; island needed 11.79 x 9.79 mm incl. escape fan-out -> DOES NOT FIT inside the minimal tile
  extending the bottom edge by +4.79 mm (south mezzanine tab) is certified by re-scan: island 12.75 x 11.00 mm at [-15.3896, 33.7201, -2.6396, 44.7201]
- **df12_pair20** (Hirose_DF12_DF12E3.0-20DP-0.5V_2x10_P0.50mm_Vertical): 20 contacts (need 22); courtyard 8.29 x 6.29 mm; island needed 9.29 x 9.79 mm incl. escape fan-out -> DOES NOT FIT inside the minimal tile
  extending the bottom edge by +4.79 mm (south mezzanine tab) is certified by re-scan: island 12.75 x 11.00 mm at [-15.3896, 33.7201, -2.6396, 44.7201]
- **gecko_pair20** (Harwin_Gecko-G125-MVX2005L0X_2x10_P1.25mm_Vertical): 20 contacts (need 22); courtyard 16.14 x 6.0 mm; island needed 17.14 x 9.5 mm incl. escape fan-out -> DOES NOT FIT inside the minimal tile
  extending the bottom edge by +4.5 mm (south mezzanine tab) is certified by re-scan: island 71.00 x 9.75 mm at [-26.3896, 34.7201, 44.6104, 44.4701]

Mezzanine stack heights the KiCad 10 library supports here: DF12 C3.0/E3.0 pairs = 3.0 mm mated. Socket depth bound is 4.94 mm, so any <= 3 mm mezzanine requires relief pockets in the chassis board under every socket; the DF12 family has 3.5/4/5 mm variants (series page) whose footprints are NOT in the KiCad library - they would need to be drawn and verified before use. The DF12 series page is flagged 'Planned End of Life'; DF40 (0.4 mm) is the family's live successor but tops out at 3.5 mm stack.

## Backplane adjacency (rev-A semantics through the chassis)

A passive backplane wires, per shared slot boundary, S.top[k] <-> slot-above.bottom[k] and S.left[k] <-> left-slot.right[k] (identical to the rev-A J102<->J103 / J101<->J104 pairing, but routed on the backplane instead of mated directly). Executable checks on a 2x2 slot field:
- [PASS] backplane node count = 4 slots x 28 tile pads  112
- [PASS] backplane adjacency matches J102<->J103 / J101<->J104 pin mapping
- [PASS] B_clk / B_data merged across bottom and right legs (one net each)
- [PASS] T_endcol/L_endrow/B_first see the neighbour GND through the backplane
- [PASS] every electrical net stays inside one of the six rev-A classes (no class-crossing wiring)  []
- [PASS] with the tile above removed, T_endcol has no GND path (reads absent)  ['T_endcol']
- [PASS] unrelated detect lines keep working when another slot is removed  ['B_first', 'GND', 'L_endrow', 'T_endcol']
- [PASS] corner slot B_first floats (no neighbour below) -> 'first' semantics kept  ['B_first']

## Presence detection (3 lines)

DET_x = 0 (present) only through the neighbour tile's strap; pull-up otherwise. GND pad in the pair is permanent backplane GND, the STRAP is not.

In addition the rev-A passive pins work unchanged through the backplane: T_endcol / L_endrow / B_first read the neighbour's GND pins, which exist only while the neighbour tile is seated (checks BK). The 3 strap lines are belt-and-braces so a slot can be sensed even with the scan logic at rest.

| line | empty | seated | half-mated (tilt along edge / toward edge / one-pad rock) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DET_T | 1 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| DET_L | 1 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| DET_B | 1 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 1 |

1 = no neighbour (pull-up floats high); 0 = neighbour present (sense pad strapped to chassis GND **through the removable neighbour tile's own copper strap**). Machine-checkable form: `out/truth_table.json`; the DET checks verify the table and the 'no permanent-GND-only path' property.

**Half-mated caveat (documented behaviour):** a neighbour tilted *towards* its strap edge can hold the strap closed while its signal pads are not yet mated; the line then correctly reports 'strap side engaged'. The tile scan protocol's marker bits still catch a non-communicating tile, as in rev A/B.

## Cost framing (one PCB per tile vs shared passive backplane)

- Tile PCB (stepped): 3542.7 mm2 x 16 tiles = 567 cm2 of small boards; the chassis backplane is cut once regardless of variant (structural + routing).
- Part-count deltas (prices not sourced here - unknown, not quoted): variant A needs chassis spring contacts (28 + 6) per slot (544 total contacts for 16 slots), tile side is copper pads only; variant B needs one connector pair per slot (32 parts over 16 slots at the chosen width) plus chassis relief pockets. The chassis board stays a passive 2-layer PCB in both variants.

64/64 passed. Full list with details: `out/checks.json`.
